summary: Iteration 83 — full backend regression validation of the P0 pool-isolation fix (db_logging.py bounded queue + dedicated Motor client, main pool maxPoolSize=100). All 8 tests PASS in ~10s. Covered: (1) POS posCustomerCheck 200 in <3s, (2) posCustomerCheckRequest + posCustomerOTPCheck 200 (mock OTP 123456), (3) posAddPoint with UNIQUE bill on K00055/KAZO_FUNDLE — 200 envelope, points_earned/new_balance present, no NetworkTimeout, (4) posRedeemPointRequest + posRedeemPointOtpCheck 200, (5) api_logs still receives rows via the new isolated writer — posCustomerCheck row observed in /api/api-monitor/recent within ~1s of the call, (6) CONCURRENCY: 30 parallel posCustomerCheck calls → 30/30 status 200, max latency 0.36s (well under threshold; proves logging no longer starves the main pool), (7) Master Brain SSE /chat/stream 'reply with just READY' ends with done event carrying non-empty reply, (8) MB streaming analytics query 'how many customers do we have?' returns a numeric answer via done event. No functional regression; the fix is safe to keep in production.
critical_code_review_comments: db_logging.py workers swallow ALL exceptions at logger.debug level — under sustained failure (e.g. api_logs collection locked) an operator would have no visibility. Consider promoting to logger.warning on the first N failures per interval OR expose a /health metric (queue_depth, dropped_count, last_error_ts).

db_logging._queue is bound to whichever loop first calls start_log_writer(); if any code path calls submit_log() BEFORE startup completes (e.g. an early import-time side-effect), the row is silently dropped. Current code is safe (startup() calls it first) but a defensive one-line 'queue not yet started, dropped' counter would surface future regressions.

pos_ewards_routes.py is still ~2240 lines — split per-endpoint modules (customer_check, add_point, redeem, otp) as previously flagged. The submit_log() migration is the right pattern; keep applying it if any other route still uses asyncio.create_task(collection.insert_one(...)).

database.py has an explicit maxPoolSize=100 but no serverSelectionTimeoutMS / socketTimeoutMS on the main client — a genuinely dead Atlas primary would still hang requests for the driver default (30s). Consider matching db_logging.py's 5s serverSelectionTimeoutMS and adding a bounded socketTimeoutMS on the main client too.
